cross_references.relationship: practical_instantiation: The survey describes APE, APO, OPRO, GRIPS in theory; the Evidently article implements a concrete optimization loop with data splitting and early stopping
performance_comparison: The survey covers multiple algorithms; LangChain article identifies PhaseEvo as most reliable and Claude-3.5-Sonnet as best engine
validation: Evidently's 40/40/20 split and dev set reliability connect to LangChain's finding that dev curves predict test performance
refinement: LangChain identifies critical overfitting risk gap in all fixed-set methods discussed in survey

gaps.description: No explicit guidance on hyperparameter tuning for beam width B, candidates K, or edits N in APO/OPRO/GRIPS
Limited detail on how to construct meta-prompts for OPRO's sorted history feedback mechanism
No comparison of computational cost between methods (APE vs APO vs OPRO vs PhaseEvo)
Insufficient guidance on threshold selection for min_score_gain early stopping criterion
No discussion of how to design verifiable labels and avoid subjective evaluation functions

metadata.processing_notes: All three cache files successfully read. Findings span all six core categories (mutation_operators, selection_strategies, scoring_evaluation, convergence_plateau, overfitting_prevention, population_management) plus four adjacent categories. Cross-references identify relationships between sources: wolfe-apo-survey provides theoretical foundation, evidently-practical demonstrates implementation patterns, langchain-optimization highlights empirical performance and limitations.
